questions.def: Use 'would have' for future in the past (reported speech).
questions.question: She said that she ___ finished the report by then.

questions.def: 'Whether' is more formal than 'if' in reported questions.
questions.question: He asked me ___ I had ever been to Japan.

questions.def: 'Deny' is followed by a gerund (-ing form).
questions.question: He ___ stealing the money.

questions.def: Backshift tense in reported speech; 'is' becomes 'was'.
questions.question: They reported that the company ___ making a profit.

questions.def: Use 'whether' for formal reported questions with 'or not' implied.
questions.question: The teacher inquired ___ all students had submitted their essays.

questions.def: Use 'said' not 'told' before 'that' without an indirect object.
questions.question: She told that she would be late because of traffic.

questions.def: Simple past tense for reported command or suggestion.
questions.question: The doctor ___ him to stop smoking immediately.

questions.def: Past continuous in reported speech: 'is going' becomes 'was going'.
questions.question: He mentioned that he ___ going to the conference.

questions.def: 'What' introduces exclamations in reported speech.
questions.question: She exclaimed ___ a wonderful surprise it was!

questions.def: 'Suggest' in reported speech is followed by a gerund phrase.
questions.question: They ___ going to the beach.

questions.def: Past perfect in reported speech (backshift of present perfect).
questions.question: The report indicated that inflation ___ risen sharply.

questions.def: 'What' introduces a reported question about a plan.
questions.question: She wanted to know ___ I intended to do after graduation.

questions.def: Use 'told' when there is an indirect object: 'He told me'.
questions.question: He said me that he was tired yesterday.

questions.def: Simple past for reported commands or warnings.
questions.question: The police ___ them not to enter the building.

questions.def: Past perfect in reported speech (backshift from past simple).
questions.question: The news reported the storm ___ caused significant damage.

questions.def: 'Whether' introduces indirect yes/no questions formally.
questions.question: They inquired ___ we needed any assistance.

questions.def: Simple past tense for reporting a statement.
questions.question: He ___ that the process was complex.

questions.def: Past perfect in reported speech (backshift from past simple).
questions.question: She claimed she ___ seen the suspect before.

questions.def: 'Whether' introduces indirect yes/no questions with 'wondered'.
questions.question: He wondered ___ the meeting had been postponed.

questions.def: Simple past to report a promise.
questions.question: He ___ he would never do it again.

questions.def: Backshift: Present simple ('is') becomes past simple ('was').
questions.question: They reported that the project ___ completed on time.

questions.def: 'Whether' is more formal than 'if' when reporting questions.
questions.question: She asked me ___ I knew anything about the incident.

questions.def: Use 'told' with an indirect object, not 'said'.
questions.question: He said me that he was going home.

questions.def: Simple past to report a complaint.
questions.question: She ___ that the service was terrible.

questions.def: Past perfect ('had') backshifts from present perfect ('has').
questions.question: The study indicated that stress levels ___ increased significantly.

questions.def: 'Whether' is formal and appropriate for reported yes/no questions.
questions.question: He asked ___ there were any questions.

questions.def: Future in the past requires 'would have' for actions completed before a future time.
questions.question: She said she ___ finished the report by then.

questions.def: Use a perfect gerund 'having worked' to describe a past action.
questions.question: He mentioned ___ late the previous night.

questions.def: When the reporting verb is past, the reported verb must also be past.
questions.question: She claimed that she has seen him yesterday.

questions.def: 'Deny' requires a past tense verb in reported speech in this context.
questions.question: He ___ having stolen the documents.
